records.narrative: Closed form from get_formula(force=true); check_explanation closed-form max abs err <= 0.0077 on train.
807 is driven by totalDayMinutes (0.63), totalEveCharge (0.22) and CSC (0.20); 1264 adds totalIntlCharge; 252 is negligible.

Local forward passes on train. The gate is a hinge in low day usage whose kink moves right with each service call above 2 (13061/12926 turn on at 3 calls). With the backbone +2.02 dayMin the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; the low-usage arm reproduces the empirical CSC>=4 x low-day churn of 0.88.

Replacing this gate by its least-squares linear fit drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model lifts 0.836 -> 0.899. It carries almost all the network s gain over linear.

params.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a low-usage hinge whose threshold rises with customer service calls (CSC). 807 = relu(-1.36 dayMin + 0.05 CSC + 0.69*2627 + 0.61*2796 - 1.30), where 2627 = 1.01 + 0.32 relu(0.87 CSC - 0.09) (always positive, affine in a CSC hinge) and 2796 = relu(0.41 - 1.00 eveCharge + 0.37 CSC + 0.15 state:41 + 0.34*12926), with 12926/13061 a two-stage CSC hinge that turns on at 3 calls. 1264 = relu(0.077 - 0.32 intlCharge + 0.39*807) adds 0.39*807 and a convex low-intl-charge hinge. Readout 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 (252 is near dead, readout -2e-5, and holds a state:2/state:44/state:4 path). Evidence (train, n=4000): sensitivity of 807 is dayMin 0.63, eveCharge 0.22, CSC 0.20. Mean gate logit rises 1.1 -> 7.4 from 0 to 7 calls. With the backbone +2.02 dayMin, the logit is V-shaped in day minutes; for CSC>=4 the low-usage arm dominates (empirical churn 0.88 low-day vs 0.24 high-day, which the network reproduces). The same hinge also lifts low-CSC, very-low-day customers (93 rows, predicted 0.17 vs empirical 0.04): a mild overextension. totalEveCharge equals totalEveMinutes after z-scoring, so the gate effectively uses evening usage. Ablation: linearising this gate drops train AUC 0.901 -> 0.851; restoring it alone on the fully linearised model gives 0.836 -> 0.899. It is the source of nearly all of the network s gain over a linear model.

params.hypothesis: Hypothesis: a service-call threshold switched off for one state. 7208 = relu(0.54 CSC - 0.37 state:49 - 0.68), readout +1.48. Active only when CSC >= 3 calls (7.6% of train rows), adding about 0.61 logit per extra call. For state:49 (one-hot z = 5.64) the pre-activation drops by 2.1, so the hinge is never active for state:49: 12 state:49 customers with CSC>=4 (5 churned, 42% vs 50% for other states) lose up to 2.75 logits. Evidence: closed form exact; linearising this unit costs only 0.002 AUC (0.901 -> 0.899) because csc_usage_gate already encodes CSC>=4. The state:49 exemption is a rare-category switch fitted to about 12 rows.

Every unit reads one (or a few) state one-hots, so it is an exact function of binary inputs and hence a constant offset per state: 10249 (state:3, -0.009 readout), 11427 (state:42, +0.05), 14942 (state:35, +0.04), 161_a (state:4, -0.03), 6730 (constant +0.43 logit except state:33, where it switches off: -0.45 logit for 77 rows), 8896 (state:19, <0.001), 3861 (state:50, dead on all rows). params.hypothesis: Root: logit P(churn) = -1.068 + linear_backbone + 1.59*807 + 1.81*1264 + 1.48*7208 - 0.88*1133 - 1.00*4051 + state offsets (+ negligible 252), purely additive in logit; the sigmoid is the only coupling. 22 inputs are unconnected (incl. totalDayCharge, totalNightCharge, totalEveCalls, totalIntlCalls, areaCode:408, 16 states) and have zero effect. Train AUC 0.901, accuracy 0.906. Performance sources (train): all children replaced by least-squares linear fits gives AUC 0.836; restoring csc_usage_gate alone gives 0.899, csc_hinge_7208 alone 0.851, voicemail_chain and state_offsets alone 0.836 (they are exactly linear on binary inputs). So the extra AUC over linear comes from the CSC x low-usage gate. Rare-category switches: backbone state:11/46/5 offsets of -2.2/-2.1/-1.4 logits on 73-80 rows (empirical -1.2/-0.8/-0.5), state:49 disabling the CSC>=4 hinge for 12 rows, state:33 offset of the wrong sign.
